subtitle: Lesson 9 · Chapter 1: Proving two Gold tables actually agree

steps.label: silver.sales_clean
steps.sub: the exact same rows feed both

code:
WITH category_rolled_up AS (
  SELECT store_id, sale_date,
         SUM(total_sales) AS rolled_up_sales
  FROM gold.category_breakdown
  GROUP BY store_id, sale_date
)
SELECT d.store_id, d.sale_date,
       d.total_sales, c.rolled_up_sales,
       ABS(d.total_sales - c.rolled_up_sales) AS diff
FROM gold.daily_sales_summary d
JOIN category_rolled_up c
  ON d.store_id = c.store_id
 AND d.sale_date = c.sale_date
WHERE ABS(d.total_sales - c.rolled_up_sales) > 0.01
caption: Roll category_breakdown back up, then compare to daily_sales_summary.

code:
rolled_up = (
    category_breakdown
    .groupBy("store_id", "sale_date")
    .agg(F.sum("total_sales").alias("rolled_up_sales"))
)

discrepancy_report = (
    daily_summary
    .join(rolled_up, on=["store_id", "sale_date"])
    .withColumn("diff", F.abs(F.col("total_sales")
                              - F.col("rolled_up_sales")))
    .filter(F.col("diff") > 0.01)
)
caption: A discrepancy report: it returns only the rows that disagree.
